source.task: Coordinate a shared Project Model contract across build-arena, elenchus-core, and arena-calibration.
source.issue: Project Model v0 parent coordination issue

goal: Keep three downstream implementation agents aligned on one pre-code decomposition contract before any repo adds incompatible F3 semantics.
nonGoals: Do not make Elenchus a truth oracle or production allow/deny gate.
Do not require child agents to run live paid model calls for acceptance.
Do not ask arena-calibration to invent the product decomposition it is supposed to test.

components.name: Contract authority
responsibilities: Publish the versioned field semantics that downstream repos must target.
Name F3 as real load-bearing reasoning aimed at the wrong target, component, sequence, or example.

components.name: Child ticket alignment
responsibilities: Ensure each child ticket names the same compatibility target and does not redefine decomposition, observable checks, or F3 locally.
Keep repo ownership explicit: build-arena emits the model, elenchus-core evaluates advisory alignment, arena-calibration proves fixture separation.

components.name: Fixture feedback loop
responsibilities: Allow calibration fixture failures to update the parent contract without letting fixture code become the product owner.
Record verification gaps and near-neighbor alternatives when the contract is too weak to classify a proposal.

dependencies.description: Child repos must target the parent Project Model v0 contract before adding local adapters or fixtures.
Child implementation gaps and fixture failures feed back into the parent contract as verification gaps or compatibility questions.

invariants.description: Elenchus signals are advisory alignment/explanation-quality evidence, not objective truth or auto-approval.
Architecture, process, and strategy components still need observable checks such as issue text, ADR review, tabletop transcript, or rubric output.

observableChecks.description: Compare docs and schema for required field names and F3 definition markers.
observableChecks.observableSignal: local tests validate worked examples against the schema and scan docs for required contract terms

observableChecks.description: Reviewer checks that non-code components have visible artifacts and evidence, not vibes.
observableChecks.observableSignal: review checklist marks each non-code component with a named artifact and pass/fail condition

observableChecks.description: Read child issue bodies and verify each names project-model/v0 plus the schema/doc compatibility target.
observableChecks.observableSignal: all child issues link to the parent and mention the same compatibility target

observableChecks.description: Verify ownership split is explicit and compatible across the child tickets.
observableChecks.observableSignal: no child issue asks elenchus-core or arena-calibration to redefine the Project Model

observableChecks.description: When a fixture exposes a contract gap, record it as a verification gap or parent compatibility question.
observableChecks.observableSignal: the parent issue/spec records the failed fixture family and proposed contract adjustment

evidenceRequirements.description: GitHub issue body excerpts proving compatibility target and ownership split.
A checklist, ADR, tabletop transcript, or process dry-run log that can be inspected by a reviewer.

assumptions.description: The build-arena parent issue is the source of truth for the shared contract during v0 rollout.
Each child repo can either validate the JSON schema directly or map its local types to the schema fields.

risks.description: Child agents may use local meanings for decomposition or observable check and pass incompatible fixtures.
risks.mitigation: Require issue bodies and acceptance criteria to target project-model/v0 explicitly.

risks.description: A vague parent model would become a bad ruler that rewards checklist matching instead of target alignment.
risks.mitigation: Run quality-gate checks for no checks, vague decomposition, missing dependencies, unclassified surface, and missing high-risk probes.

nearNeighborAlternatives.description: Let each repo define its own compatible-looking Project Model shape.
nearNeighborAlternatives.whyNotPrimary: The repos would drift on F3 and observable-check semantics before calibration can compare results.

nearNeighborAlternatives.description: Ask arena-calibration to create F3 fixtures before build-arena defines the model contract.
nearNeighborAlternatives.whyNotPrimary: Calibration fixtures need a stable ruler; otherwise they test local guesswork instead of product intent.

heldOutProbes.scenario: A child issue uses local names such as projectObjective and validationEvidence while claiming compatibility.
heldOutProbes.expectedBehavior: The parent compatibility check flags the missing schemaVersion/project-model/v0 target and requires a mapping or issue edit.

heldOutProbes.scenario: An architecture component is described as important but has no ADR, issue body, checklist, or other inspectable artifact.
heldOutProbes.expectedBehavior: The quality gate flags no observable check or unclassified surface instead of accepting the strategy prose.
